candidates: In example and tutorial scripts, use matplotlib's object-oriented interface (`fig, ax = plt.subplots()` followed by `ax.plot(...)`, `ax.set_xlabel(...)`, `ax.set_ylabel(...)`, `ax.legend()`, etc.) rather than the pyplot global-state interface (`plt.plot(...)`, `plt.xlabel(...)`, etc.). The global-state API relies on mutable module-level state and makes examples harder to reason about; `plt.show()` at the end is acceptable.
